claim: In the winter of 1891 a 30-year-old physical education instructor from the International YMCA Training School in Springfield, Massachusetts invented an indoor game, basket ball.

evidence.quote: In the winter of 1891, when a 30-year-old physical education instructor from the International YMCA Training School in Springfield, Massachusetts invented an indoor game that could be played between football and baseball seasons, basket ball, originally two words, was born.

claim: Naismith settled upon a game that required two teams, two peach baskets, a ball, and thirteen rules.

evidence.quote: After trying several different ideas, he settled upon a game that required two teams, two peach baskets, a ball, and thirteen rules.

claim: Naismith's secretary typed up the rules and tacked them on the bulletin board.

evidence.quote: Naismith then drew up the 13 original rules, which described, among other facets, the method of moving the ball and what constituted a foul. A referee was appointed. The game would be divided into two, 15-minute halves with a five-minute resting period in between. Naismith’s secretary typed up the rules and tacked them on the bulletin board.
evidence.locator: Where Basketball Originated, paragraph on rules

claim: Naismith set up the first basketball game with two peach baskets in a gymnasium at the International YMCA Training School (now Springfield College) in Springfield, Massachusetts in December 1891.

evidence.quote: In the roughly three-minute clip, Naismith, who had traveled to New York for a basketball doubleheader at Madison Square Garden, discusses setting up the first basketball game with two peach baskets in a gymnasium at the International YMCA Training School (now Springfield College) in Springfield, Massachusetts in December 1891.

notes: Bears on baseline tmp-baseline-F-13 (game created at Springfield College): the institution was then the International YMCA Training School.

claim: Luther Halsey Gulick, Naismith's supervisor and the College's first physical education director, challenged Naismith to invent a new indoor game for the School's students to play during the long New England winter.

evidence.locator: Where was Basketball Invented?, closing paragraph

evidence.quote: Urged by Luther Halsey Gulick, the college’s superintendant of the physical department, to create a new indoor game “that would be interesting, easy to learn, and easy to play in the winter and by artificial light,” Naismith responded.
